headline: Treat parent links as another edge in a breadth-first search
statement: Given a binary tree, an existing target node, and nonnegative k, return values of every node whose shortest edge distance from target is exactly k. Values are unique and output order is unrestricted. Trainer input identifies target by value. Distance counts edges, so the target itself has distance zero.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
constraints: Node values are unique integers from 0 through 500.
0 <= k <= 1000; target exists in the tree.
intuition: From the target, a move may go to a child or to a parent. First remember parent links, then use a queue to expand outward from the target one edge at a time. Mark visited nodes so moving back along an edge does not repeat them.
approach: Traverse from root to build the parent map.
Start a queue with (target,0) and mark target seen.
For nodes at distance k, collect values without expanding further.
For closer nodes, enqueue unseen child and parent neighbors at distance+1.
correctness: The parent map adds exactly the reverse of each tree edge. BFS in this undirected graph first reaches each node by its shortest path from target, while seen prevents repeats. Every node at distance k is collected once; no farther nodes are expanded or returned.
bruteForce: For each node separately find its path from target and measure it, requiring up to O(n^2) work.

complexity.explanation: The parent map, seen set, traversal stack, and BFS queue store at most a linear number of nodes.

pitfalls: Include parent moves; a subtree-only traversal misses answers.
Do not expand nodes already at distance k.
